 Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 10-02-2020 at about 3.00 p.m., near the tea stall of Tippanaik, at Mariyammanahalli village, Hosapete taluka, Bellari District, the car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MW-0357, belonging to the respondent No.2 was involved in an accident and the petitioner who was the occupant of said vehicle has sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Hosapet, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Aster R. V. Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was an engineer and was doing part time work as a freelancer and earning a sum of Rs.35,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Mariyammanahalli Police have registered the case against the driver of the car bearing No.KA-05-MW-0357 for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer, respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 3 have appeared through their counsel.
The respondent No.1 has filed its written statement.
The respondent No.2 did not choose to file written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.3 remained absent and hence, he is placed ex-parte.

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing No.KA-05-MW-357 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicle Act.

It has denied the occurrence,
mode of the accident and involvement of the car bearing No.KA-05-MW- 357 by the alleged driver,
as alleged in the claim petition.
It has contended that, the driver of the offending car was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
The respondent No.2 has willfully entrusted his vehicle to the person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle, as on the date of accident.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 10- 02-2020 at about 3.00 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing registration No.KA-05-MW-0357 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?

3 . What order or Award?
6.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to 12.

Further, he has got examined one more witness namely Dr. S.
Ramachandra as P.W.2 and closed his side.
On the other hand, the respondents No.1 and 3 have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

sentences.text: Issue No.1:

It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 10-02-2020 at about 3.00 p.m., near the tea stall of Tippanaik, at Mariyammanahalli village, Hosapete taluka, Bellari District, the car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MW-0357, belonging to the respondent No.2 was involved in an accident and the petitioner who was the occupant of said vehicle has sustained grievous injuries.
Earlier to the accident, he was an engineer and was doing part time work as a freelancer and earning a sum of Rs.35,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to 12.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is discharge summary, Ex.P.2 is final bill, Ex.P.3 is x-ray,
Ex.P.4 is copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.5 is copy of first information statement, Ex.P.6 is copy of charge-sheet,
Ex.P.7 is copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.8 is copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.9 is copy of sketch, Ex.P.10 is C.T. scan report, Ex.P.11 is out-patient record and Ex.P.12 is CT scan film.

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.4 to 9, prima-facia it reveals that, on 10-02- 2020 at about 3.00 p.m., near the tea stall of Tippanaik, at Mariyammanahalli village, Hosapete taluka, Bellari District, the petitioner was traveling in the car bearing Reg.No.KA- 05-MW-0357, belonging to the respondent No.2.
At that time the driver of said car drove the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the one Ravinaik, who was standing near the tea stall of Tippanaik and turtle the said car.
Due to said impact, the said Ravinaik and the inmates of said car namely the petitioner Rakesh, Shivakumar and Varun sustained grievous injuries.
The said Ravinaik succumbed to the injuries on spot.
Whereas, the other injured were shifted to hospital in 108 ambulance.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his Ex.P.6 final report/charge-sheet that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-MW-0357.
12.

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident and involvement of car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-MW-0357 in the alleged accident are not in dispute.

Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner and driver of offending vehicle i.e., respondent No.2 & 3, as they did not choose to contest the case of petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.1 insurance company though has specifically denied the above said facts in its written statement, it has not produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Even,
the respondent No.1 insurance company has not stepped into witness box to depose the contentions taken in its written statement on oath.
Though the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

It is pertinent to note that, at one point in his cross-examination the P.W.1 has admitted that, at the time of accident the said car was being driven by one Sachin and he had given statement to the Police with respect to same.

But, the said admission clearly seems to be stray admission, because in the beginning of cross-examination itself Rakesh.M vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156096997/
4 the petitioner has clearly stated that, he do not know who is the owner of offending car bearing Reg.
No. KA-05- MW-0357 and who was driving the said car at the time of accident.

sentences.text: It really the offending car was being driven of alleged Sachin and not by the respondent No.3 and the petitioner has given statement with respect to same before the Police, the respondent No.1 would have easily proved the same by producing the copy of alleged statement of the petitioner.
But, the respondent No.1 has neither produced the alleged statement of the petitioner in the case, nor it has adduced any evidence with respect to same.

Non production of said document to the Court by the respondent No.1, leads this Court to draw adverse inference against the respondent No.1 and hold that, there is no such statement given by the petitioner before the Police and the above admission is just a stray admission.
Further, the petitioner/P.W.1 has unequivocally denied all the suggestions made to him in the cross-examination.

13. Further, the Ex.P.8 spot mahazer and Ex.P.9 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the extreme left side of Hosapete-Kudalagi NH-50 national highway road, infront of Tippanaik tea stall, at the distance of 20 feet from the said tea stall, situated at Mariyammanahalli village, Hosapete taluka, Bellari District, due to dashing of offending car bearing Reg. No. KA-05- MW-0357 to deceased Ravinaik, who was standing near the tea stall of Tippanaik and turtle of said car.
Further, it is not the case of respondent No.1 that, the said accident is caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the said accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending and no other vehicle was involved in the accident,
then in the given facts and circumstances of the case it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence of the driver of offending car bearing No. KA-05- MW-0357.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his Ex.P.6 final report/charge-sheet that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car bearing No.KA-05-MW-0357.
Admittedly, the said charge-sheet is not challenged by the owner or the driver of the offending vehicle.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing has been elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident is not caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.KA-05-MW-0357.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle, the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
There is absolutely no material on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent No.1 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-MW-0357.
14.

Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.1 discharge summary,
Ex.P.3 X-ray, Ex.P.10 CT scan report, Ex.P.11 out-patient record and Ex.P.12 CT scan film, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the road traffic accident and he has suffered L1- (1st lumber) D8, D10 dorsal or thoracic/vertebral compression fracture with intact posterior elements.
The same is deposed by P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.

On the other hand, there is no rebuttal Rakesh.M vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156096997/
5 evidence produced by the respondent No.1, to show that the above medical records are false documents.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.1 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-MW-0357 and the injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

sentences.text: 16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the reasons stated above, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that,
he has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, occurred on 10-02-2020 at about 3.00 p.m., near the tea stall of Tippa Naik, at Mariyammanahalli village, Hosapete taluka, Bellari District,
due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-MW-0357.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-MW-0357 and he has sustained grievous injuries i.e. L1- (1st lumber) D8, D10 dorsal or thoracic/vertebral compression fracture with intact posterior elements.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.,

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has not produced any relevant document.
In the petition, his age is shown as 22 years, as on the date of accident.
Likewise, in all the medical records, produced and got marked by the petitioner as Ex.P.1 and 2, his age is mentioned as 22 years.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is not specifically denied by the respondent No.1 and even not seriously disputed in the cross-examination of the petitioner.

Even, there is no contrary material on record, which creates doubt on the oral evidence of the petitioner or to disbelieve the above documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is considered as 22 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered L1- (1st lumber) D8, D10 dorsal or thoracic/vertebral compression fracture with intact posterior elements.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries sustained by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner is having permanent physical disability of 13.71% to the whole body.
The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.1 discharge summary, Ex.P.3 x-ray, Ex.P.10 CT scan report, Ex.P.11 out-patient record and Ex.P.12 CT scan film clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained the above stated grievous injuries.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to him and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 10-02-2020 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 27-11- 2023,
which is after lapse of three years and nine months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner not undergone any surgery and he had been treated conservatively.
Further, he has clearly admitted that, as per the opinion of treated doctor there is no neurological deficit to the petitioner.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.3 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the lumber 1st vertebra shows anterior wedge compression fracture in the range of upto 50% and fractures of 8th to 10th thoracic vertebra shows residual compression.

Therefore,
considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was an engineer and was doing part time work as a freelancer and earning a sum of Rs.35,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has not produced any document to prove that, before accident he was an engineer and was doing part time work as a freelancer and earning a sum of Rs.35,000/- per month.
Further, he has clearly admitted in his cross- examination that, he was working as an assistant in the office of his friend by name Rahul and he was paid Rs.15,000/- per month.
Now he is working as an Engineer in LTI Mind Tree Company and earning a sum of Rs.17,000/- per month.
This clearly goes to show that, the petitioner has continued his job and the disability suffered by him has not affected his work.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for loss of future income due to permanent disability suffered by him does not arise at all.

For the disability suffered by the petitioner, he can claim compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort, but not under the head loss of future income due Rakesh.M vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156096997/
7 to disability.

sentences.text: Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head loss of future income.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, due to injuries sustained in the accident, he has incurred huge expenses towards the medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
In order to prove the same, he has produced final bill, as per Ex.P.2.
The said bill has been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spend total amount of Rs.70,000/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, in such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.70,000/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

As per the medical records placed on record, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e., L1- (1st lumber) D8, D10 dorsal or thoracic/vertebral compression fracture with intact posterior elements.
As per Ex.P.1 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken conservative treatment as in-patient for 09 days from 11-02-2020 to 19-02-2020, in Aster RV Hospital, Bengaluru.

Further, as per the evidence of P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of his disability, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.30,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:

As per Ex.P.1 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken conservative treatment as in-patient for 09 days from 11-02-2020 to 19-02-2020, in Aster RV Hospital,
Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 9 = Rs.9,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:

As per Ex.P.1 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken conservative treatment as in-patient for 09 days from 11-02-2020 to 19- 02-2020, in Aster RV Hospital,
Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount for food and nourishment during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs. 800 x 9 = Rs.7,200/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Bahubali Nagar, near Water Tank,
Jalahalli, Bengaluru, the accident has taken place near the tea stall of Tippanaik, Mariyammanahalli village, Hosapete taluka, Bellary district and he has taken treatment at Aster RV Hospital,
Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between all the above three places

,
compensation of Rs.4,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 09 days as in-patient at Aster RV Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
But, the petitioner has not produced any document to show that, he has sustained loss of income during treatment period.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for loss of income during treatment period does not arise at all.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under this particular head.

sentences.text: It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 22 years and unfortunately he has suffered fracture of weight bearing bones.
The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 8% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has not stated anything with regard to requirement of any further treatment to the petitioner and future medical expenses.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.

Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.
19.

1. Loss of future income -Nil- 2.

9. Future medical expenses -Nil-
Total Rs
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,40,200/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer, respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending car bearing Reg. No. KA-05- MW-0357 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.

Therefore,

However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,40,200/- from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,40,200/- (Rupees one lakh forty thousand two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest awarded to petitioner shall be released in his favour through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

But, the said admission clearly seems to be stray admission, because in the beginning of cross-examination itself Rakesh.M vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156096997/
4 the petitioner has clearly stated that, he do not know who is the owner of offending car bearing Reg.
No. KA-05- MW-0357 and who was driving the said car at the time of accident.
It really the offending car was being driven of alleged Sachin and not by the respondent No.3 and the petitioner has given statement with respect to same before the Police, the respondent No.1 would have easily proved the same by producing the copy of alleged statement of the petitioner.
But, the respondent No.1 has neither produced the alleged statement of the petitioner in the case, nor it has adduced any evidence with respect to same.
Non production of said document to the Court by the respondent No.1, leads this Court to draw adverse inference against the respondent No.1 and hold that, there is no such statement given by the petitioner before the Police and the above admission is just a stray admission.
Further, it is not the case of respondent No.1 that, the said accident is caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.
When the said accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending and no other vehicle was involved in the accident,
then in the given facts and circumstances of the case it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence of the driver of offending car bearing No. KA-05- MW-0357.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle, the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
There is absolutely no material on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent No.1 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-MW-0357.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.1 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-MW-0357 and the injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.,
The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has not produced any relevant document.

Even, there is no contrary material on record, which creates doubt on the oral evidence of the petitioner or to disbelieve the above documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is considered as 22 years.
Therefore,
considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for loss of future income due to permanent disability suffered by him does not arise at all.
For the disability suffered by the petitioner, he can claim compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort, but not under the head loss of future income due Rakesh.M vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156096997/
7 to disability.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head loss of future income.
But, the petitioner has not produced any document to show that, he has sustained loss of income during treatment period.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for loss of income during treatment period does not arise at all.

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,40,200/- (Rupees one lakh forty thousand two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest awarded to petitioner shall be released in his favour through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
